concepts.def: Charles I governed for eleven years without calling Parliament, raising money through devices such as Ship Money and fines.
Disputes over religion, including Laud's reforms and the Scottish Prayer Book rebellion, plus money and royal power, led to war between king and Parliament in 1642.
Royalists fought Parliamentarians across England; Parliament's New Model Army won the decisive victory at Naseby in 1645.
Charles I was tried for treason and beheaded in January 1649; the monarchy and House of Lords were abolished and England became a republic.
Oliver Cromwell ruled as Lord Protector from 1653 to 1658, campaigning in Ireland and Scotland and briefly imposing the Rule of the Major-Generals.
Charles II was invited back as king in 1660; his reign included the Plague of 1665, the Great Fire of 1666 and the Exclusion Crisis before his death in 1685.

mcqs.q: Which army won the Battle of Naseby in 1645?
options: Parliament's New Model Army
The Royalist army under Prince Rupert
The Scottish Covenanters fighting for the king
The Irish Confederate army

mcqs.q: What happened to Charles I in January 1649?
options: He was tried for treason and publicly beheaded
He escaped into exile in France
He was imprisoned for life in the Tower
He was killed in battle at Worcester
The monarchy was restored and Charles II returned as king
Oliver Cromwell became Lord Protector
The Civil War began
James II was overthrown

mcqs.q: Was the Civil War a war between England and Scotland?
options: Cromwell ruled as the elected president of a parliamentary democracy.
The English Civil War was a war of England against Scotland.
The Civil War was fought between England and Spain.
No - it was a civil war within the kingdoms between supporters of the king and of Parliament, though Scottish armies intervened on different sides at different times.

mcqs.q: Did Oliver Cromwell make himself king?
options: No - he refused the crown when Parliament offered it in 1657 and ruled instead as Lord Protector until his death in 1658.
Cromwell ruled as the elected president of a parliamentary democracy.
Cromwell was crowned King Oliver after the Civil War.
The Restoration abolished Parliament permanently.

mcqs.q: Did the Restoration simply turn the clock back to 1629?
options: In 1660 royal power was restored exactly as it had been under Charles I's Personal Rule.
No - Charles II returned by invitation, most opponents were pardoned under the Act of Indemnity, and kings could no longer ignore Parliament as Charles I had tried to.
The Restoration abolished Parliament permanently.
Cromwell ruled as the elected president of a parliamentary democracy.
